joinPassword.playersSetAPasswordThe: Players set a password the first time they join and give it every time after. Worth having when Mojang authentication is off, because without it the server has only a name to go on and anyone who knows a listed name can use it.
joinPassword.bedrockHasNoEquivalentIt: Bedrock has no equivalent. It loads neither plugins nor mods, so the player list and the addresses it is bound to are what closes this server.
joinPassword.thisServerRunsNeitherPlugins: This server runs neither plugins nor mods, so there is nothing to install. Switch it to Paper, or to a mod loader, from Settings first.
joinPassword.theirPasswordCanAppearIn: Their password can appear in the server log, which the Console screen shows - it is hidden only by a library Modrinth does not carry, so treat these as passwords for this server and nothing else.
joinPassword.playersWillDrop: {count, plural, one {# player is} other {# players are}} connected and will be disconnected.
joinPassword.restartsToApply: The server restarts to apply it.
joinPassword.noAnswer: Polaris did not answer. Reload the page and try again.
joinPassword.modOn: Everybody registers with /register the next time they join. While the server cannot reach Polaris, nobody can join and it does not start.
joinPassword.modOnListed: Everybody registers with /register the next time they join, and the passwords kept by {name} stop working. While the server cannot reach Polaris, nobody can join and it does not start.
joinPassword.modOff: Anybody on the player list gets in on their name alone afterward. The passwords stay here in case you turn it back on.

joinPassword.noBuildFor: {name} has no build for the release this server runs ({version}). The server would start without it and nobody would be asked for a password, so this is left off rather than left looking on.
joinPassword.guardOn: Everybody sets their own the next time they join.
joinPassword.guardOff: Anybody on the player list gets in on their name alone afterward.
joinPassword.foreign: Players already log in with <mono>{name}</mono>, which Polaris does not manage. Remove it from the Mods screen to use a login from here instead.
joinPassword.usesLogin: Uses Polaris login: players get <mono>/register</mono> and <mono>/login</mono> with text passwords, kept in Polaris so you can reset one here. While the server cannot reach Polaris, nobody can join and the server does not start.
joinPassword.still: Players still log in with <mono>{name}</mono>. Turning this on replaces it, and every player registers again.
joinPassword.stillNumeric: Players still log in with <mono>{name}</mono> and numeric passwords. Turning this on replaces it, and every player registers again.
joinPassword.installs: Installs <mono>{name}</mono> from Modrinth, which the Mods screen shows afterward like anything else on the list. A release it has no build for is skipped and the server starts without it rather than failing to start, so check the Mods screen once the server is back up.
joinPassword.triggerHelp: Players register with <mono>/trigger register set 1234</mono> and come back with <mono>/trigger login set 1234</mono>. The password can only be a number: this runs as a data pack, and the only thing vanilla lets an unauthenticated player send the server is a scoreboard value. Writing <mono>/trigger register</mono> without <mono>set</mono> does not fail - it registers the password 1, and the next login says the password is wrong.
joinPassword.pluginHelp: Players register on their first join with the commands <mono>{name}</mono> documents on its Modrinth page. Tell them before turning this on: nobody can look that up from inside the server they have just been locked out of.

On by default; a server made before it gets it on its next start. While it is on, the server downloads it from this Polaris each time it starts, and does not start if Polaris cannot be reached.

mining-rush.label: Mining rush
mining-rush.summary: Most ore mined in the time wins. Any ore scores by its rarity, or pick diamonds or ancient debris only. Players caught by Anti X-Ray or the anti-cheat during it are left off the podium.

mob-hunt.label: Mob hunt
mob-hunt.summary: Most hostile mobs killed wins, the rare and dangerous ones worth more, or a single kind of mob.

supply-drop.label: Supply drop
supply-drop.summary: A chest of loot lands somewhere in the Overworld. Where is revealed in three steps, a beam of light marks it, and the first player to open it keeps what is inside.

blood-moon.label: Blood moon
blood-moon.summary: Night falls with rain and waves of mobs rise around every player on the surface. Survive to dawn without dying; the podium goes to the most kills.

world-boss.label: World boss
world-boss.summary: A boss drawn at random appears near the players, in a sky arena or on open ground. It fights in three phases, with warned attacks and a shield of minions, and grows with every fighter. If it falls, the most damage wins - or the final blow, if chosen - everybody who hit it is rewarded, and the winner earns a trophy.

fishing.label: Fishing contest
fishing.summary: Most catches with a fishing rod wins.

trivia.label: Trivia
trivia.summary: Questions about Minecraft, or a scrambled word, in the chat. The first right answer takes the round. Add questions of your own.

explorer.label: Explorer
explorer.summary: Travel the farthest on foot, swimming, riding or gliding - or race to a set of coordinates announced at the start.

happy-hour.label: Happy hour
happy-hour.summary: Haste, luck and other effects for everybody for a while. No winner - a good filler between competitions.

king-of-the-hill.label: King of the ring
king-of-the-hill.summary: Who joins is brought to a ring floating in the air, fists only, where nobody can die. Time in the ring scores, and three times as much alone in it, so pushing the others out pays; over each round it shrinks and moves, and the one ahead wears a crown.

treasure-hunt.label: Treasure hunt
treasure-hunt.summary: Loot chests are hidden on open ground around the players, each under a column of light, and everybody's action bar points to the nearest. Whoever opens the most wins, and keeps what is inside.

gathering.label: Gathering
gathering.summary: A few short rounds, each for one material announced as it starts - wheat, logs, cobblestone, iron... Every item is worth points by how hard it is to get, and the most points over all rounds wins. Nothing is taken from anybody.

rare-catch.label: Rare catch
rare-catch.summary: A fishing race for one treasure - a name tag, a saddle, an enchanted book... The first to fish it up wins, and keeps it.

xp-boost.label: Experience boost
xp-boost.summary: Extra experience for every mob killed and every ore mined, for everybody, for a while. No winner - a good filler between competitions.

waves.label: Horde defense
waves.summary: A defense point is marked away from every home and waves of monsters come for it, each bigger and better armored than the last, with jockeys among the last ones. Everybody who holds the point is rewarded; the podium goes to the most kills, or the most damage if chosen.

meteor-shower.label: Meteor shower
meteor-shower.summary: Meteors of ore fall one after another on open ground away from every home, each marked by a beam of light. Whoever mines the most meteor blocks wins.

parkour.label: Parkour race
parkour.summary: A jump course is built high in the air: rows climbing back and forth, or a tower climbed round and round. Players type join in the chat to take part and are taken to the start; the fastest to the finish wins, a fall only sends you back to your last checkpoint, and no platform can be reached but the next one.

spleef.label: Spleef
spleef.summary: The floor is lava: a snow floor is built high in the air, and each run is played one of the ways switched on - shovels that break only that snow, a floor that vanishes under your feet, or snowballs that break it. Whoever falls through is out and sent back; the last one standing wins.

team-duel.label: Team duel
team-duel.summary: Players who type join are split into two teams in an arena built in the sky, each given the same sword and shield. The team with more eliminations wins; the podium goes by each player's own. Nobody loses anything: a player low on health is sent back to their side, and inventories are kept whatever happens.

build-battle.label: Build battle
build-battle.summary: Players who type join each get a plot in the sky, a theme and a kit of colored glass. When the time is up everybody tours the plots and votes for the best in the chat. Only the kit can be built with; nothing of anybody's is used or taken.

tnt-run.label: TNT run
tnt-run.summary: Floors of TNT are stacked high in the air, and every block a player steps on vanishes a moment later. Keep running: fall through a floor and you land on the one below, fall through the last and you are out. The last one standing wins; nothing explodes.

boat-race.label: Ice boat race
boat-race.summary: A walled track of ice is built in the air and every racer gets a boat at the start. Pass every gate in order - a gate missed does not count - and the first to finish the laps wins. Fall off or lose the boat and you are put back at your last gate with a new one.

dropper.label: Dropper
dropper.summary: A deep shaft is built in the air with floors that have holes in them and a pool of water at the bottom. Players fall from the top through the holes; landing on a floor sends you back to the top, and the fastest into the water wins. Nobody takes fall damage.

capture-the-flag.label: Capture the flag
capture-the-flag.summary: Players who type join are split into two teams in an arena built in the sky, with a base and a banner at each end and cover in between. Carry the other team's banner home while yours is there to capture it; the carrier glows, and drops it when brought low. The captures set win it early, or the most when time is up. Nothing of anybody's is lost.

hide-and-seek.label: Hide and seek
hide-and-seek.summary: A manor is built in the sky, bigger the more who play, its rooms drawn anew each time: a library, a forge, a garden with a waterfall, a pond, mazes and more. Its walls hide rooms behind paintings and panels that open from across the room, with a button, a rug or a stare; there are cellars under the floor, a hollow tree and lava only hiders can cross. The seekers wait, blinded, while the others hide; a seeker's hit finds a hider, who then seeks too. Hiders score for every second hidden and seekers for every hider found; names are hidden from the other side.

hot-potato.label: Hot potato
hot-potato.summary: Players who join stand on a small platform in the sky, and one is handed the potato: TNT on their head, glowing. Hit somebody to pass it on. When the fuse runs out whoever holds it is out and the next round starts; the last one left wins. Nobody is hurt.

sky-wars.label: SkyWars
sky-wars.summary: Each player who joins starts alone on an island of their own floating in the sky, with chests of gear and blocks; a bigger island in the middle holds better loot. Bridge across, fight, and be the last one left. Falling or dying only puts you out - everybody's own things are kept and given back.

village-defense.label: Villager defense
village-defense.summary: A villager is set at a point on the ground and waves of monsters come for it. Keep it alive to the last wave: if it dies the event ends and nobody wins. The most kills top the podium, and nothing is lost if you die.

bingo.label: Bingo rush
bingo.summary: Everybody gets the same card of nine items, drawn for the run. An item counts once it is in your inventory, and each one scores; the first full line or full card - whichever is set - ends it. Easy cards hold things found in the first minutes, hard ones take a trip.

boss-fishing.label: Boss fishing
boss-fishing.summary: A legendary fish takes the line and everybody fishing wears it down: each catch takes a share of its strength off the boss bar, and treasure takes more. Land it in time and whoever caught the most wins; let it get away and nobody does.

nether-maze.label: Deadly nether maze
nether-maze.summary: A roofed maze of netherrack is built in the air, a new one every time. Racers start outside its door; the first to reach the bright room in the middle wins. Fire, magma and lava never hurt, but touching them sends you back to the start.

acid-rain.label: Acid rain
acid-rain.summary: An open arena is built in the air, and an acid rain falls on it alone. Standing with nothing over your head fills your acid bar; full, you are out. Shelter in the ruined huts or build your own with the cobblestone handed out, while the rain eats it away. The last one left wins.

facts.regeneration: Regeneration (health comes back on its own)
facts.happyHour: Everybody on gets {effects} until it ends, including whoever joins meanwhile.
facts.chestsHidden: {count} {count, plural, one {chest} other {chests}} hidden up to {distance} blocks from the players, on open natural ground well away from anybody's bed.
facts.clues: A column of light stands over every chest nobody has opened, from the start, and every player's action bar shows how far the nearest one is and which way. The chat says only how many there are and who opens each.
facts.chestsCleared: Chests are spread round the players, each sought its own way and kept apart. A chest is only put where there is air or a small wild plant, which is put back; one nobody opened is taken away at the end. An opened chest stays: what is inside is the finder's.
facts.materialRandom: Each round's material is drawn from the list, never one an earlier round had, and announced only as the round starts.
facts.gatheringScore: Scored by what each player holds at the end minus what they held when it began, and never more than they picked up during it - a stack taken out of a chest does not count. Nothing is taken from anybody.
facts.rareCatch: The first player to fish up {treasure} wins, and keeps it. Taking one out of a chest, or dropping one and picking it up, does not count.
facts.xpBoost: Everybody on gets {extra} until it ends. Nothing is ever taken away; an ore block placed during it is not paid for again.
facts.waves: {waves} waves, {minutes} minutes at most. A wave ends when all of it is killed, or after two minutes.
facts.wavesPoint: The point is on open, flat ground the world made, at least 96 blocks from any online player's bed. Only monsters that cannot break blocks come - no creepers, endermen or ravagers - and every one of them is removed when it ends.
facts.keepInventory: Keep inventory is on while it runs, so dying costs nothing; the server's own setting comes back afterward.
facts.meteors: {meteors} meteors of {size} ore blocks each, one every {seconds} seconds from the start. Each block mined near a meteor scores 1; ore placed near one is taken off.
facts.meteorsLand: Meteors land on open, flat ground the world made, away from every online player's bed - on an island, on the island itself - and ore is only ever put where there was air. What nobody mined is taken away at the end - only blocks still exactly the meteor's ore - and nothing else is touched.
facts.pickaxes: Diamond and emerald ore need an iron pickaxe, ancient debris a diamond one.
facts.parkour: {jumps} jumps, {difficulty}, built about {height} blocks up. A fall lands on a net and goes back to the last checkpoint.
facts.spleef: A {size} by {size} snow floor about {height} blocks up. Falling through it is being out; the last one on it wins.
facts.joinCountdown: Only players who type join (or unirse) in the chat during the countdown - at least {seconds} seconds - take part. They are taken there and brought back to exactly where they were when it ends, even after a restart.
facts.stageBuilt: It is built only in empty air, over open ground away from everybody's bed, and taken down block by block afterward - only what it placed. Inside, nobody can take damage and everybody is in adventure mode; their game mode is given back after.
facts.spleefShovel: Players get a marked shovel that only breaks the snow; it is cleared at the end, and nothing else of theirs is touched.
facts.tntRun: {layers} floors of TNT, {size} by {size}, stacked about {height} blocks up. Every block a player stands on goes a moment later; falling through a floor lands on the next, and through the last is being out. The last one standing wins.
facts.tntRunSafe: Nothing explodes: the blocks are only ever taken away, and any TNT lit near the arena is put out at once. Played by a small data pack Polaris adds to the world.
facts.boatRace: {laps} {laps, plural, one {lap} other {laps}} of an ice track about {height} blocks up: a new loop every time, walled on both sides, with gates to pass in order. Fall off, cut a corner or leave your boat and you go back to your last gate in a new one.
facts.boatRaceBoats: Every racer starts with a boat, taken back at the end. The gates are counted by a small data pack Polaris adds to the world.
facts.dropper: A shaft of {levels} floors, {difficulty}, each with one hole that never lines up with the one above it, and a pool at the bottom. A new shaft every time, and every hole reachable from the one above while falling.
facts.dropperSafe: Played under Slow Falling, so there is time to steer and no fall hurts. Landing on a floor is caught the moment it happens by a small data pack Polaris adds to the world.
facts.duelJoin: Only players who type join (or unirse) in the chat during the countdown take part. They are split into two teams and taken to an arena built 30 blocks up, over open ground away from anybody's bed.
facts.duelKit: Everybody gets the same {kit} sword and a shield. A player down to {hearts} {hearts, plural, one {heart} other {hearts}} is out: the other team scores, the rival who brought them down gets the elimination, and they are sent back to their side, healed. The team with more wins; the podium goes by eliminations.
facts.duelKeepInventory: Keep inventory is on while it lasts and put back after, so even a death in the arena keeps everything.
facts.duelNeeds: Needs Player versus player allowed in Settings. Up to 16 players.
facts.buildJoin: Only players who type join (or unirse) in the chat during the countdown take part. Each gets a plot on a platform built 30 blocks up, over open ground away from anybody's bed.
facts.buildPlanMine: A theme from your list, a {size} by {size} plot, 16 kinds of glass and a brush; {minutes} minutes to build, then {seconds} seconds touring the plots and voting in the chat - one vote each, not for your own plot. Most votes wins.
facts.buildPlanBuiltIn: A built-in theme, a {size} by {size} plot, 16 kinds of glass and a brush; {minutes} minutes to build, then {seconds} seconds touring the plots and voting in the chat - one vote each, not for your own plot. Most votes wins.
facts.buildGlass: Only the kit's glass can be placed: builders play in adventure mode, where their own blocks cannot be put down at all, so nothing of theirs is used or left on a plot. Glass broken by hand drops nothing, so no kit leaves a plot either.
facts.arena: Nothing of anybody's is touched. The arena goes only where the air was empty, and comes down block kind by block kind; only the event's own marked kit is taken back; each player is sent back to exactly where they stood, in their own game mode, with whatever they dropped. Somebody offline at the end finds it still standing when they log in, and is sent back then.
facts.overworld: Happens in the Overworld; only players there take part.
facts.rankedFrom: Ranked from {score} {unit}; below that, no podium and no prize.
facts.startsWith: Starts on its own only with {count} {count, plural, one {player} other {players}} actually playing, and not while somebody is in a fight.
facts.hostileMobs: Needs the server above Peaceful, where hostile mobs exist.
facts.unrankedAfk: Nobody playing in creative or spectator, caught by the anti-cheat, or AFK the whole time is ranked.
facts.unranked: Nobody playing in creative or spectator, or caught by the anti-cheat, is ranked.
facts.needsPlayers: {count, plural, one {Needs # player on the server.} other {Needs # players on the server.}}
facts.needsJoiners: {count, plural, one {Goes ahead with # player joined.} other {Goes ahead with # players joined, or is called off.}}
facts.bossDrawn: A boss drawn at random each time from: {bosses}.
facts.bossFight: {difficulty}. Three phases: from two thirds of its health, minions shield it until they are killed; from one third, it rages. Every attack is warned a second before it lands, and its health grows with every fighter.
facts.bossArena: Fought in a closed glass arena built only into empty air 30 blocks over open ground, away from every bed, and taken down afterward. A beam of light takes players up; there they play in adventure mode, and at the end they are put back at the beam, even after a restart or when they next log in.
facts.bossGround: Fought on open ground away from every bed. Nothing it does breaks or places a block, and it cannot be trapped: it comes to whoever it cannot reach.
facts.bossKeeps: Keep inventory is on while it runs, so dying costs nothing, and pets, horses and villagers near it take no damage. The server setting comes back afterward, even after a restart.
facts.bossGriefing: Mob griefing is off while {bosses} fights, so no block is changed. The server setting comes back afterward, even after a restart.
facts.bossPrizes: Prizes are multiplied by {times} on this difficulty.
facts.bossWinnerDamage: The most damage dealt to it wins. Every fighter sees their own damage during the fight, and everybody's is listed at the end.
facts.bossWinnerFinalBlow: Whoever lands the final blow wins; the rest are placed by the damage they dealt, which each fighter sees during the fight.
facts.bossTrophy: The winner also gets a trophy: a Nether Star named after the boss.
facts.bossBeam: The beam of light up to the arena is announced with its coordinates, and everybody not up yet sees how far it is and which way.
facts.wavesScaling: Each wave brings the first wave's size, half as many again for every wave before it and for every defender at the point past the first (up to 5), at most 60. Every defender past the first gives each monster 4 more health (up to 16), and from 3 defenders they hit harder.
facts.wavesGear: Armor grows wave by wave, from none to leather, chainmail, iron and diamond on the last, with enchanted bows and swords on the last two. Spider jockeys come from 40% of the waves, chicken jockeys from 60% and horsemen from 80%. Nothing they wear or ride is ever dropped, and all of it is removed.
facts.gatheringRounds: {rounds} {rounds, plural, one {round} other {rounds}} of {minutes} {minutes, plural, one {minute} other {minutes}}. Each item is worth points by how hard it is to get - one cobblestone 1, one log 4, one iron ingot 12 - and the most points over all rounds wins.
facts.world: {time, select, day {Holds midday} night {Holds midnight} other {Leaves the time alone}}{weather, select, clear { and clear weather} rain { and rain} other {}} while it runs, then gives the time back and lets the weather change again.
facts.netherMaze: A {size} maze about {height} blocks up, with {hazards} of its rooms on fire, on magma or behind a lava pit. Walls two blocks thick and a solid roof: it cannot be climbed or seen over, and every room can be reached without touching a hazard.
facts.netherMazeSafe: Nobody's items are touched, and nobody takes damage. Minimap cave view and radar are switched off for the racers. The hazards are watched by a small data pack Polaris adds to the world.
facts.acidRain: A {size} arena about {height} blocks up, with {acidity} rain. The world's own weather is never changed: the rain falls only over the arena.
facts.acidRainSafe: Nobody's items are touched, and nobody takes damage. Players get marked cobblestone that only goes on the arena, taken back when they leave. The rain is worked out by a small data pack Polaris adds to the world. Needs Minecraft 1.17 or later.

editor.healthComesBackOnIts: Health comes back on its own.
editor.fistsOnlyHint: Players join and come with nothing: their things are kept and given back after, nobody can die, and pushing wins the circle.
editor.ringRoundsHint: 1 to 5. The time is split between them; each starts with the ring whole, everybody back on their spot, and its end counts double.
editor.ringShrinksHint: A block at a time over each round, down to what the players need: two blocks round the middle for two, four for sixteen.
editor.ringMovesHint: It drifts over the platform a block every few seconds, so nobody holds it standing still.
editor.2To12ForOne: 2 to 12 for one defender; each wave and each defender adds more.
editor.onlyVillagerHunters: Only monsters that go for villagers, and nothing that breaks blocks.
editor.neverCreepersEndermenOrAnything: Never creepers, endermen or anything else that breaks blocks.
editor.between50And1000Around: Between 50 and 1000. Around the players, or around the coordinates.
editor.parkourShapesHint: One of those switched on is drawn each time it runs.
editor.easyWidePlatformsShortGaps: Easy: wide platforms, short gaps. Hard: single blocks, gaps of up to three.
editor.name: Name
editor.whatPlayersSeeInTitles: What players see in titles and on the scoreboard.

editor.emptyPlaceGetsTheRest: Left empty, it gets what everybody else does.

editor.plotSizeHint: 7 to 15 a side, as tall as it is wide
editor.themesHint: One a line; one is drawn each time.
editor.builtInThemes: One of 30 built-in themes, in the players' language.
editor.materialHint: Drawn anew for each round, never one an earlier round had, and announced as the round starts. Only what is gathered during the round counts.
editor.catchHint: One treasure comes up about once in 120 catches, any of them about once in 25 - in open water, more often with Luck of the Sea. Give it 20 minutes or more.
editor.perKillHint: Experience points, 0 to 100. A zombie gives 5.
editor.perOreHint: Experience points, 0 to 100. Coal ore gives up to 2.
editor.minPlayersJoined: Called off when fewer join during the countdown.
editor.minPlayersOnline: It does not start with fewer players on the server.
editor.bossDifficultyHint: Epic by default. A harder boss has more health, hits harder, attacks more often and pays more.
editor.skyArenaHint: A closed glass arena built into empty air 30 blocks up and reached through a beam of light, so nothing of the fight reaches the ground. The Wither fights only here.
editor.bossPoolHint: One of these is drawn each time it runs.
editor.bossPoolEmpty: Keep at least one boss that can fight here.
editor.witherNeedsArena: The Wither fights only in the sky arena.
editor.baseHealthHint: 100 to 1024: its health for one fighter on Normal. Harder levels and every fighter who joins raise it.
editor.bossWinnerHint: Most damage counts every hit by hand, and shares what the boss loses to arrows, tridents and magic among whoever is shooting it. Final blow: whoever fells it wins, and the rest go by damage.
editor.bossTrophyHint: A Nether Star named after the boss, with a glint and its difficulty, on top of the prizes. Only when the boss is defeated.
editor.spleefWaysHint: One of those switched on is drawn each time it runs.
editor.dropFloorsHint: 5 to 20. Harder means smaller holes, further apart.
editor.capturesToWinHint: 1 to 10. Otherwise the team with more when time is up wins.
editor.hideSecondsHint: 15 to 90, before the seekers can move.
editor.seekersHint: 1 to 3. Everybody found seeks with them.
editor.fuseSecondsHint: 10 to 40 before the potato goes off.

editor.bingoItemsHint: Easy: found in the first minutes. Hard: needs a trip to the Nether.
editor.fishCatchesHint: 3 to 30 for each player fishing: more players, a bigger fish.
editor.mazeHazardsHint: How many rooms have fire, magma or a lava pit.
editor.acidityHint: How fast the rain fills a bar and eats a shelter.

announcements.appliesOnJoin: Takes effect as each player next joins. No restart needed.
announcements.stopped: Start the server to check its mods.
announcements.none: No mod on this server announces itself.

announcements.readFailed: Could not read the server's mods.

chat.title: Chat moderation
chat.intro: Lines that break these rules are stopped before anybody sees them, and the player is told why in their language.
chat.needsAnticheat: Chat moderation runs in Polaris's anti-cheat, which is off on this server. Turning it on restarts the server to load it.
chat.unsupported: Nothing Polaris runs on this server can stop a chat line: vanilla Minecraft has no way to. It works on Paper, Purpur, Spigot and Folia, and on NeoForge 1.21.4.
chat.installDetail: It carries chat moderation. The server restarts to load it, and anybody playing is disconnected for a moment.
chat.installed: Anti-cheat on. The server is restarting.
chat.askManager: Somebody who manages this server can turn it on.
chat.seen: Moderating: the server took these rules <time></time>.
chat.advertisingHint: An IP address, or a host name like play.example.net, also when spelled with "dot".
chat.allowedDomainsHint: One per line: this server's own address, a partner's. Their subdomains are allowed too.
chat.floodHint: More than 5 lines in 5 seconds, or more than the limit a minute.
chat.repeats: The same line again and again
chat.repeatsHint: The same line more often than this in two minutes.
chat.linksHint: Any http, https or www address.
chat.capsHint: Lines of 8 letters or more, nearly all capitals.
chat.wordsHint: One word or phrase per line. Accents, capitals and digits for letters are seen through.
chat.strikesHint: After {strikes} stopped lines in 10 minutes the player is timed out for {minutes} min, recorded as a sanction.
chat.neverTimeout: Players are only warned, never timed out.
chat.badDomain: Allowed addresses are host names or IPs, one per line.
chat.saved: Saved. The server takes it within 30 seconds.
chat.readFailed: Could not read the chat rules.
chat.saveFailed: Could not save the chat rules.

loader.title: Mod loader
loader.heldHint: Every start runs this version without asking {loader}'s repository.
loader.followingHint: Each start asks {loader}'s repository for the newest version. Polaris pins the installed one once the server is up.
loader.releaseHint: Minecraft is set to the newest release, so there is no single {loader} version to pin. Choose a release under Settings to pin it.
loader.customHint: The installer is yours, so there is nothing to pin.
loader.updating: The next start installs the newest {loader}, and Polaris pins it again once the server is up.
loader.confirmBody: The server downloads the newest {loader} from its repository on its next start. If that repository is down or answers in a format this server cannot read, the server will not start until it recovers. Mods built for {version} may not load on the new version.
loader.updateQueued: The newest {loader} installs the next time the server starts.
loader.updateStarted: The server is restarting with the newest {loader}.
